method: bench/perf_suite.py --quick on the same machine (fingerprint below); 'before' = one run immediately before the optimisation commit, 'after' = median of 3 runs after. Quick mode, n=300: indicative, not a gating measurement.

findings_C065.finding: kernel traversed each argument twice per step (bounds check inside _within_bounds and again inside _arg_ref)
typing.Mapping in hot isinstance checks: ~85 __instancecheck__/__subclasscheck__ calls per invoke
retry engine built a new random.Random() (urandom seeding) on every call: 3 per invoke
lineage recomputed for every run event
findings_C065.action: fixed: cached per (config generation, topology snapshot, minute)

findings_C065.finding: redaction iterated 12 secret fragments and 4 regexes per field
~9 json.dumps per invoke (two hash chains + telemetry copy)
findings_C065.action: kept: both chains are required (kernel PK_AGENT_STEP/1 and run-event PK_AGENT_RUN_EVENT/1); documented duplicate audit levels

findings_C065.finding: argument canonicalised twice (kernel HMAC arg_ref + unkeyed sha256 for idempotency key)
findings_C065.action: kept deliberately: the kernel key is per-process, so a failover executor could not match a committed effect; the unkeyed digest is what makes replay suppression survive failover

findings_C065.finding: one runtime-wide RLock around the event chain serialises all tenants; 8 threads are slower than 1
findings_C065.action: open: shard the chain per tenant or batch appends (needs ADR; affects audit ordering semantics)

findings_C065.finding: 0 hops in-process: adapters are local; real hop count depends on INV-57/59/70/71 deployment
completed runs and events retained forever (~18 KB/run) — found by soak
findings_C065.action: fixed: GovernedRuntime.archive() bounded retention (INV-69-owned growth FLAT in soak_with_archive)
